articles.title: Nuh Raids Seize 7,600 kg of Suspected Synthetic Paneer Headed for Delhi-NCR
articles.excerpt: Overnight raids on four unlicensed units in Haryana's Nuh district recovered tonnes of suspected analogue paneer and the chemicals used to make it, in a crackdown aimed at the Delhi-NCR wholesale food chain.
articles.image_caption: A block of paneer with cut cubes on a wooden board. The image accompanies coverage of the September 10-11 raids in Nuh, Haryana, where officials seized nearly 7,600 kg of suspected synthetic paneer.
articles.nri_angle: Diaspora readers visiting Delhi-NCR should know cheap bulk paneer in catering and informal markets may be adulterated; genuine paneer lists only milk and acidulants, and the risk is concentrated in unregulated wholesale channels, not branded products at home or abroad.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Inside Elder, Sujan Sarkar's British-Indian Chophouse Reinventing New York Dining
articles.excerpt: The Michelin-starred chef behind Indienne has opened Elder, an à-la-carte British-Indian chophouse at Hudson Yards' Henry Hall — and it may be the clearest sign yet of Indian cuisine's new confidence in America.
articles.image_caption: Chef Sujan Sarkar stands in the open kitchen of Indienne at Henry Hall in New York. He has opened Elder, a British-Indian chophouse, downstairs in the same building.
articles.nri_angle: Elder turns Indian cooking into the house cuisine of a New York dining destination, reflecting the Indian-American dining scene's move from curry-house familiarity to confident, mixed-table ambition.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: FDA Suspends Mumbai Eatery's Licence After Diner Allegedly Finds Rat in Dosa
articles.excerpt: Radhakrishna Hotel in Borivali West lost its food licence after a customer said he found a dead rat in his Mysore masala dosa — the latest flashpoint in FDA chief Tukaram Mundhe's festive-season crackdown.
articles.image_caption: A masala dosa served with chutney and sambar. The FDA suspended a Mumbai eatery's licence after a diner allegedly found a rat in a dosa.
articles.nri_angle: Mumbai's restaurant scene is a pilgrimage stop for visiting NRIs; the crackdown is a reminder that even beloved legacy eateries can fail basic hygiene checks, so diners should trust FSSAI compliance over reputation.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Clermont's Guru Indian Restaurant Marks 12 Years of Northern Indian Classics
articles.excerpt: Master Chef Uday Kadam's family-run Clermont eatery celebrates a dozen years of tandoor-fired favorites — and expands next door with The Venue, a new event space and Sunday brunch.
articles.nri_angle: Master Chef Uday Kadam's journey from a village near Mumbai to Disney to Central Florida — and his restaurant's role as a community gathering place — shows how Indian restaurateurs have become cultural anchors in American suburbs.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Recheado Masala: The Fiery Goan Red Paste Every Seafood Lover Should Know
articles.excerpt: Born of Goa's Portuguese heritage, this tangy red masala of chillies, spices and vinegar is the soul of the coast's stuffed-fish fries — and it keeps for days in the fridge.
articles.image_caption: A bowl of recheado masala, the red spice paste of dried red chillies, spices, garlic, tamarind and vinegar. In Goa the paste is traditionally stuffed into mackerel and pomfret before shallow-frying.
articles.nri_angle: Recheado masala is a staple of Goan Catholic kitchens worldwide, and the vinegar-based paste travels well — a make-ahead taste of home for diaspora cooks.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: This 70-Year-Old Hyderabad Shop Bottles Biryani Into a Pickle
articles.excerpt: Qadeem Achar Ghar in Murgi Chowk spent two months perfecting a 20-ingredient, fully vegetarian biryani-flavoured achaar — built for expats missing home.
articles.image_caption: Avakaya, the spicy Andhra mango pickle — the 70-year-old Hyderabad shop sells a biryani-flavoured take on it.
articles.nri_angle: The biryani pickle was created specifically for expats missing the taste of home, and the shop ships vacuum-sealed packs with online ordering.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: From Chole Kulcha to Rogan Josh: Australian Couple's One-Day Amritsar Food Run Wins the Internet
articles.excerpt: The couple hit Pehelwan Kulcha, Beera Samosa Wala, Gian Di Lassi and Surinder Meat Shop in a single day — and say it's only day one of their journey.
articles.image_caption: Chole kulcha, a highlight of the Australian couple's one-day Amritsar food run.
articles.nri_angle: For Punjabi NRIs, the Amritsar food trail is a map of homesickness — the couple's stops are the landmarks diaspora families describe when they talk about going back.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Beyond the Espresso: How India's Cafés Are Winning Customer Loyalty
articles.excerpt: Food now adds 55% more revenue per customer than beverages alone, and India's cafés — from work cafés to creative studios to craft brands like Subko — are building loyalty through experience, not just espresso.
articles.image_caption: India's café chains are winning customer loyalty with localised menus and community spaces.
articles.nri_angle: The café boom mirrors third-wave coffee culture in the US and UK with a distinctly Indian accent — modern cafés are now a fixture of NRI homecoming itineraries, and the experience-led loyalty playbook is transferable to diaspora-run café ventures abroad.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: From Rs 18 Lakh Debt to Rs 2 Crore Sales: A Chole Bhature Miracle
articles.excerpt: A tiny Chembur eatery was Rs 18 lakh in debt and about to close — then Abhishek Upmanyu's Instagram tip and Anushka Sharma's order for Virat Kohli turned Delhi Se into a four-outlet, Rs 2-crore-a-month brand.
articles.image_caption: Delhi Se, a 250-square-foot chole bhature outlet in Mumbai’s Chembur, now sells 3,000-plus plates a day.
articles.nri_angle: The Delhi Se turnaround shows how Indian celebrity culture can transform a small business overnight — a dynamic the diaspora watches closely, since Punjabi eateries are among the most common immigrant small businesses in the US, UK and Canada.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Harsh Goenka Savours 10-Course Vegetarian Menu at World's No. 1 Restaurant Maido
articles.excerpt: At Maido in Lima — No. 1 on the World's 50 Best Restaurants 2025 — chef Mitsuharu Tsumura created his first-ever 10-course vegetarian tasting menu, and Goenka called it memorable.
articles.image_caption: Harsh Goenka, chairman of RPG Group, shared his meal on X on September 28, 2026. He dined at Maido in Lima, Peru, ranked No. 1 on the World's 50 Best Restaurants 2025 list.
articles.nri_angle: An Indian vegetarian billionaire celebrating a plant-based tasting in Lima — a city whose Nikkei cuisine was built by the Japanese diaspora — ties two food-migration stories together.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Revant Himatsingka Quit a Rs 2 Crore US Job to Become the Food Pharmer
articles.excerpt: Speaking at NDTV Yuva 2026, the food and health activist explained why 13 years in the US convinced him that India needs better health literacy around packaged food.
articles.image_caption: Revant Himatsingka, known as Food Pharmer, left a Rs 2 crore consulting job in the US to raise awareness about packaged food.
articles.nri_angle: Himatsingka's story mirrors a growing pattern of NRIs leaving high-paying US careers to work on problems back home — here, India's packaged-food crisis.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Jaipur's Amber Terrace Named Among World's 25 Best New Hotel Restaurants
articles.excerpt: Amber Terrace, the rooftop Pan-Asian lounge at The Leela Palace Jaipur, is the Indian entry on Travel + Leisure's ranking of the world's 25 best new hotel restaurants, chosen from 120 venues across 17 countries.
articles.image_caption: The Hawa Mahal in Jaipur, Rajasthan. The Leela Palace Jaipur's rooftop lounge Amber Terrace was named among Travel + Leisure's 25 best new hotel restaurants in the world.

sources.label: US Times Mirror (Travel + Leisure list coverage)
Hospitality Tip of the Day (Nouvelle Vague guest shift)

articles.nri_angle: A globally ranked rooftop in Jaipur gives overseas Indians visiting Rajasthan a marquee dining stop on the winter wedding-season circuit.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Parag Milk Foods to Invest ₹100 Crore, Quadruple Paneer Capacity to 80 Tonnes a Day
articles.excerpt: The dairy maker will expand plants in Maharashtra and Andhra Pradesh by June 2027, betting on the shift from unorganized to branded paneer. Paneer has grown 28% for the company in two years.
articles.image_caption: Rows of fresh paneer cubes move along a production line at a dairy plant. Parag Milk Foods plans to quadruple its paneer capacity to 80 metric tonnes per day by June 2027 with a ₹100 crore investment.
articles.nri_angle: Branded Indian paneer is expanding globally — Parag's Dairy Valley brand recently launched in UK supermarkets — so the capacity expansion supports the diaspora's growing access to familiar, high-quality dairy.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: High-Protein Spinach Paneer Wrap Packs 26g Protein in 460 Calories
articles.excerpt: Instagram food creator Shagun Malhotra shared her paneer wrap recipe on September 17 — spiced paneer slabs and crunchy vegetables inside a spinach-based wrap, aimed at vegetarians trying to stay fitter in their 30s and beyond.
articles.image_caption: A paneer wrap filled with spiced paneer, lettuce and sliced vegetables. The photo illustrates the recipe Instagram creator Shagun Malhotra posted on September 17, which she says packs 26 g of protein into 460 kcal.
articles.nri_angle: Protein intake is a common worry for Indian vegetarian families abroad, and this wrap offers a familiar, home-cookable answer at a claimed 26 g per serving.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Kachoris and Coffee: Why Food Has Become the New Fuel for India's Run Clubs
articles.excerpt: Across Indian cities, post-run kachoris, modak and tiramisu have turned sunrise runs into the new social outing for a sober-curious generation.
articles.image_caption: An India Today illustration shows runners alongside modaks, kachoris and tiramisu. India's run clubs are pulling in members with post-run food spreads, from dawn kachori runs to tiramisu meetups.
articles.nri_angle: Diaspora run clubs already end long runs at dosa joints and chai carts, and NRIs visiting India can use local run clubs as a low-barrier way to build a social circle.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Delhi Destroys 2,800 Kg of Adulterated Sweets and Dairy Ahead of Festive Season
articles.excerpt: Delhi's Food Safety Department has stepped up inspections at mandis, sweet manufacturing units and markets across the capital, putting paneer, khoya and ghee under scrutiny as festive-season demand surges.
articles.image_caption: Coiled jalebis at an Indian sweet shop. Delhi food safety officials destroyed 2,800 kg of adulterated sweets and dairy ahead of the festive season.
articles.nri_angle: For Indian families marking the festive season abroad, the drive is a reminder that paneer, khoya and sweets — the staples of every festival table — are most vulnerable to adulteration when demand surges, so buying from licensed sellers matters.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Diwali Sweets Will Cost More as Ghee, Sugar and Dry Fruit Prices Climb
articles.excerpt: Sweet shops across India are preparing to pass on surging ingredient costs this festive season — and shoppers may pay more or get smaller boxes.
articles.image_caption: Indian sweets displayed at a mithai shop. Sweet makers expect festive-season prices to rise as much as 15% as sugar, milk, ghee and dry fruit costs climb.
articles.nri_angle: NRIs celebrating Diwali abroad face the same squeeze — mithai in Edison, London or Dubai costs more to make and gift this season.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: The Sando Project brings Japanese milk-bread sandos to Chennai and Puducherry
articles.excerpt: Ciclo Café's limited-time Sando Project menu piles Indo-Chinese chilli chicken, bibimbap paneer and beef fillet with mustard into thick, in-house Japanese milk bread across Chennai and Puducherry.
articles.image_caption: Japanese milk bread. Ciclo Café's limited-time Sando Project menu builds sandos on in-house shokupan in Chennai and Puducherry.
articles.nri_angle: For diaspora families visiting Chennai or Puducherry this season, The Sando Project is a fresh, limited-time stop worth adding to the eating itinerary between home cooking and old favourites.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: From Curry Clubs to Beer Gardens: Indian Food Finds Home in English Pubs
articles.excerpt: From village pubs in Worcestershire to London locals hosting Diwali parties, Indian food festivals are drawing crowds to some of England's most traditional drinking spots.
articles.image_caption: A traditional pub interior. Indian food festivals and curry nights are increasingly finding a home in pubs across England, from Wetherspoon's Thursday Curry Club to London Diwali celebrations.
articles.nri_angle: The pub curry night is one of the most visible ways Indian food culture has woven itself into everyday British life — and a reminder of the diaspora restaurateurs and traders behind it.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Skip the Pricey Sweet Shops: Make Soft No-Cook Kaju-Pista Modak at Home
articles.excerpt: No gas, no mava, no sugar syrup — this cashew-and-pistachio modak comes together in a mould in under 30 minutes, just in time for Ganeshotsav.
articles.image_caption: Kaju-pista modaks arranged on a brass plate before a Ganesha idol during Ganeshotsav. The no-cook recipe uses cashew and pistachio doughs kneaded with powdered sugar, milk powder and cardamom.
articles.nri_angle: For diaspora families celebrating Ganeshotsav far from India's mithai shops, this no-cook modak delivers an authentic prasad with ingredients available at any international grocery store.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Viral Video Reveals Spiti Monastery Kitchen Where Monks Cook From 1 AM
articles.excerpt: Monk Ten Zin's viral video shows the 1 a.m. kitchen routine inside a Spiti monastery — giant bolep korkun rotis, rotating menus of biryani and fried rice, and teamwork over ceremony.
articles.nri_angle: For diaspora viewers who picture monastic life as pure austerity, the videos offer an affectionate, humanizing glimpse of Himalayan Buddhist kitchen life.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: New Barossa Restaurant The Curry Lab Revives Forgotten Indian Spices in Nuriootpa
articles.excerpt: Run by 24-year-old Shan and his parents, the Nuriootpa restaurant pairs family recipes with an interactive spice library where diners can smell the ingredients behind the menu.
articles.image_caption: The interior of The Curry Lab in Nuriootpa. The family-run restaurant opened on September 17 with a menu built around lesser-used Indian spices.
articles.nri_angle: For South Australia's Indian community and curious locals, The Curry Lab brings regional Indian cooking beyond the standard curry-house repertoire into wine country.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Rohit Sharma's Match-Night Comfort Food: His Mother's Banana Wafers
articles.excerpt: The former India captain revealed on his new show 'Family Full House' that Test-match nerves kept him awake at night — and that his mother's homemade, baked banana wafers were the comfort food he always carried with him.
articles.image_caption: Rohit Sharma smiles during a public appearance. The former India captain revealed on his new show that his mother's homemade banana wafers were his comfort food during sleepless Test-match nights.
articles.nri_angle: For the diaspora, Rohit Sharma's banana-wafers confession is a familiar story — a mother's homemade snack as the one taste of home no hotel kitchen or foreign supermarket can replace.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk
